text:
A: Hi! Hello, can you hear me?
B: I can, yeah. Gary.
A: Hi Gary, I'm Elira. I'm in Walthamstow, in London.
B: London. Right.
A: Ha, you said that like it was bad news.
B: No, no. Long way, that's all. I'm Hucknall, Nottingham. What do you do, me duck?
A: Erm, I'm sort of between jobs at the moment. I was an office coordinator for a property management company, and they restructured, so I took voluntary redundancy. I'm applying for office manager jobs now, and doing a bookkeeping course.
B: Voluntary. So they paid you to go.
A: Kind of, yeah. It wasn't really voluntary, though, they merged my role either way. Sorry, that sounds defensive.
B: No, take the money, I would. Only, to be fair, there's work about if you want it. Our place is always after people.
A: Yeah, no, I'm applying for loads. It's just, I want the right thing, you know? Somewhere small where I'm not just a number.
B: Hm. Small places are better. Big firms, it's all who's mates with the manager.
A: Oh, a hundred percent. What do you do?
B: Setter-operator, injection moulding. Twenty-two year at the same place. Lowest scrap rate on the line.
A: Twenty-two years! That's amazing. I don't think anyone stays anywhere that long now.
B: No. They don't. Mortgage is nearly done, couple more year. Bought it off the council in the nineties, put an extension on the back myself.
A: Yourself? Like, the actual building?
B: Me and a mate, he's a brickie. Six metre across.
A: Okay, I'm impressed. At my old job I used to chase builders for quotes and they'd just never ring back.
B: That'll be the contractors you was using. I ring people back. I do fences and sheds weekends, and I'm round when I say.
A: Honestly, you'd have been my favourite. Erm, what else do you do? Holidays?
B: Tenerife, most years. All-inclusive. Booked a year out.
A: Oh, I've been to Tenerife! Girls' trip. Which bit?
B: Costa Adeje. Same hotel, four year running. You know what you're getting.
A: That's so nice, though. I'm a planner too, I make a shared note with all the flight times and everything, my boyfriend Callum thinks I'm mad.
B: Callum. Not the one off this?
A: No! Ha, no, a different Callum. Did you have him?
B: I did. Talked about my steel for ten minutes. Nice enough lad.
A: Ha, yeah, he seemed nice. Erm, where were we? Food! What do you have for dinner?
B: Tea. On the table half five. Meat and two veg, Sunday dinner without fail.
A: See, that's the thing I keep getting told off for today, everyone says tea. My mum would do stuffed peppers or pite, that's like a pastry, Albanian. I'm trying to learn hers.
B: Albanian. I've not had that.
A: It's good, honestly, like cheese and spinach in loads of thin layers. You'd like it, it's filling.
B: Filling I can do. Julie's on at me to watch my weight, mind.
A: Oh, well, don't tell her I said.
